title: A Border for the Contact
premise: Wendell Underhill, a private security contractor with a fabricated past, is approached by a stranger claiming Wendell once saved her life — a favor he never performed. The debt she repays is a dossier proving that the diplomatic summit he's been hired to protect is built on a staged assassination plot, one his own employer authored. Hunted by an assassin who knows his real name and squeezed between loyalty to his crew and the truth he's uncovered, Wendell smuggles the evidence across three jurisdictions to expose the conspiracy before the summit convenes. In the end, he testifies under his true identity — the lie abandoned at last — trading his career for the truth, while the stranger vanishes, her debt paid.
about_author: Cyrus Yarrow is a former logistics coordinator for international summits who writes thrillers drawn from the gray zones between governments and private contractors. He lives near a land border he refuses to name, where he collects maps of places that no longer exist.

chapters.title: The Favor That Never Was
chapters.summary: POV: Wendell. Between contracts in a border city, Wendell is cornered by Mara Voss, a stranger who insists he saved her life in Sarajevo — an event he knows never happened. She leaves him a sealed dossier as 'interest' on the debt. Reading it, he finds evidence his current employer orchestrated a false-flag killing planned for the upcoming summit. Emotional beat: unease curdling into dread as his polished lie starts cracking.

chapters.title: Interest Owed
chapters.summary: POV: alternating Wendell and Mara. Wendell verifies the dossier's claims while his own team is quietly reassigned — witnesses being positioned, or removed. Mara resurfaces, revealing she manufactured the favor deliberately: she needed a man inside the summit's security whose loyalties were purchasable. The assassin, Codrin, makes first contact, killing a colleague and leaving Wendell's real birth certificate on the body. Emotional beat: betrayal compounding betrayal; trust becomes currency neither can afford.

chapters.title: Three Borders, One Truth
chapters.summary: POV: Wendell. With Codrin hunting them and both governments' agencies compromised, Wendell and Mara run the evidence across three borders using the smuggling routes only contractors know. Each crossing costs something — a contact burned, a cover shredded, Mara wounded. They learn the plot's final piece: the assassination is scheduled for the summit's opening hour, with Wendell's own crew as deniable instruments. Emotional beat: exhausted resolve; loyalty to people vs. loyalty to truth made literal at every checkpoint.

chapters.title: The Contact
chapters.summary: POV: Wendell, closing with Mara. At the summit perimeter, Wendell must choose: warn his crew and lose the evidence window, or deliver the dossier to a neutral delegate and let events unfold. He does both — triggering the evacuation that exposes the plot mid-attempt, forcing Codrin's failure and capture. Testifying under his birth name, Wendell surrenders the polished lie forever. Mara disappears, debt settled. Emotional beat: catharsis through self-erasure; identity finally owned rather than performed.
